questions.prompt: Assessment used during teaching to guide the next learning steps is primarily assessment ____ learning.
questions.explanation: Formative assessment helps teachers and learners decide what to improve next. Its main purpose is to support learning while it is happening.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 2, 31 and 32; clarification: https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/assessment/basics/formative-summative.html

questions.prompt: A teacher checks learners’ understanding halfway through a lesson and adjusts the teaching. What kind of assessment is this?
questions.explanation: The check is being used to improve ongoing teaching and learning, which makes its purpose formative.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 2, 31 and 32; clarification: https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/assessment/basics/formative-summative.html

questions.prompt: Which assessment primarily evaluates achievement at the end of an instructional unit?
questions.explanation: Summative assessment evaluates what learners have achieved at the end of a unit against the intended standard.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 2, 31 and 32; clarification: https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/assessment/basics/formative-summative.html

questions.prompt: Which is the clearest example of formative assessment?
options: A final examination used only for a final grade
A certificate awarded after completing school
An exit question used to plan tomorrow’s teaching
questions.explanation: The exit question supplies feedback that changes the next lesson. The use of that feedback, rather than the question format, is what makes the assessment formative.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 2, 31 and 32; clarification: https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/assessment/basics/formative-summative.html

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of feedback in formative assessment?
options: To identify learning gaps and guide improvement
To guarantee every learner the same grade
To prevent learners from trying again
questions.explanation: Useful formative feedback identifies what is understood, what needs work and the next steps for improvement.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 2, 31 and 32; clarification: https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/assessment/basics/formative-summative.html

questions.prompt: Can results from a summative test also be used formatively?
options: Yes, if they guide later teaching and learning
No, test results can only assign grades
Only if every learner gets full marks
Only if the test has no questions
questions.explanation: A final test can serve a summative purpose for grading and also inform later revision. Assessment purpose depends on how the evidence is used.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 2, 31 and 32; clarification: https://www.cmu.edu/teaching/assessment/basics/formative-summative.html

questions.prompt: Which learning domain primarily concerns attitudes, values and feelings?
questions.explanation: The affective domain covers attitudes, feelings and values. This clarifies the book’s short answer “manner”.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 1, 23, 25 and 34; clarification: https://www.vumc.org/nursing-contact-hours/writing-objectives and https://teaching.cornell.edu/resource/blooms-taxonomy

questions.prompt: Which learning domain primarily concerns physical skills and coordinated movement?
questions.explanation: Psychomotor learning concerns physical performance and motor skills. Knowledge about a skill is different from actually performing it.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 1, 23, 25 and 34; clarification: https://www.vumc.org/nursing-contact-hours/writing-objectives and https://teaching.cornell.edu/resource/blooms-taxonomy

questions.prompt: Which learning domain primarily concerns knowledge and thinking?
questions.explanation: Cognitive learning includes remembering, understanding and other intellectual processes.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 1, 23, 25 and 34; clarification: https://www.vumc.org/nursing-contact-hours/writing-objectives and https://teaching.cornell.edu/resource/blooms-taxonomy

questions.prompt: How many broad learning domains are commonly distinguished in the cognitive, affective and psychomotor framework?
questions.explanation: There are three broad domains in this framework. The six levels often discussed within the cognitive taxonomy are a different classification.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 1, 23, 25 and 34; clarification: https://www.vumc.org/nursing-contact-hours/writing-objectives and https://teaching.cornell.edu/resource/blooms-taxonomy

questions.prompt: In the original cognitive taxonomy, combining ideas into a new plan is most closely associated with which level?
questions.explanation: Synthesis combines elements into a new whole, such as a proposed plan. The revised taxonomy uses “create” for the related category.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 1, 23, 25 and 34; clarification: https://www.vumc.org/nursing-contact-hours/writing-objectives and https://teaching.cornell.edu/resource/blooms-taxonomy

questions.prompt: A learner demonstrates a practical skill accurately. Which domain is most directly being assessed?
questions.explanation: A practical demonstration directly assesses performance of a physical skill, placing the focus on the psychomotor domain.
questions.source: Model Aptitude Test for GES 1, Child Development and Pedagogy, questions 1, 23, 25 and 34; clarification: https://www.vumc.org/nursing-contact-hours/writing-objectives and https://teaching.cornell.edu/resource/blooms-taxonomy
